'''Lloyd Nicholas Trefethen''' (born 30 August 1955) is an American mathematician, professor of [[numerical analysis]] and until 2023 head of the Numerical Analysis Group at the [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford]].<ref name="scopus">{{Scopus|id=7003930041}}</ref><ref name="googlescholar">{{GoogleScholar|9hvCdiQAAAAJ}}</ref><ref name="dblp">{{DBLP|name=Lloyd N. Trefethen}}</ref><ref name="howfast">{{Cite journal | last1 = Nachtigal | first1 = N. L. M. | last2 = Reddy | first2 = S. C. | last3 = Trefethen | first3 = L. N. | doi = 10.1137/0613049 | title = How Fast are Nonsymmetric Matrix Iterations? | journal = SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications | volume = 13 | issue = 3 | pages = 778 | year = 1992 }}</ref> He was elected a Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web | title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and International Members - NAS | url=https://www.nasonline.org/news/2025-nas-election/ | access-date=2025-08-18 | website=nasonline.org}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Trefethen was born 30 August 1955 in [[Boston, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/americanmenwomen07jaqu|url-access=registration|title=American Men & Women of Science: Physical and Biological Sciences|date=1986|publisher=Bowker| last1=Hollister | first1=D. | last2=MacFarland | first2=Scott |others=Jaques Cattell Press.|isbn=0835222217|edition=16th|location=New York|pages=[https://archive.org/details/americanmenwomen07jaqu/page/n201 184]|oclc=13680380}}</ref> the son of mechanical engineer [[Lloyd M. Trefethen]] and codebreaker, poet, teacher and editor [[Florence Newman Trefethen]].<ref name="whoswho"/> Trefethen attended [[Phillips Exeter Academy]].

He obtained his bachelor's degree from [[Harvard College]] in 1977 and his master's from [[Stanford University]] in 1980. His PhD was on ''Wave Propagation and Stability for Finite Difference Schemes'' supervised by [[Joseph E. Oliger]] at [[Stanford University]].<ref name="mathgene"/><ref name="trephd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Lloyd Nicholas|last=Trefethen |title=Wave Propagation and Stability for Finite Difference Schemes |publisher=Stanford University |year=1982 |author-link=Lloyd N. Trefethen|oclc=9136203|id={{ProQuest|303229499}}}}</ref><ref name="acm">{{ACMPortal|id=81100259928}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Following his PhD, Trefethen went on to work at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] in New York, [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and [[Cornell University]], before being appointed to a chair at the [[University of Oxford]] and a Fellowship of [[Balliol College, Oxford]].<ref name="SNC">{{cite web |url=http://www.orcca.on.ca/conferences/snc2007/site/talks/talks.html|title=SNC '07 Invited Speakers|access-date=26 April 2008}}</ref>

His publications span a wide range of areas within numerical analysis and applied mathematics, including non-normal [[eigenvalue]] problems and applications, spectral methods for differential equations, [[numerical linear algebra]], [[fluid mechanics]], computational [[complex analysis]], and approximation theory.<ref name="pubs">{{cite web |url=http://web.comlab.ox.ac.uk/people/Nick.Trefethen/publication/publication.html |title=Nick Trefethen publication list}}</ref> He is perhaps best known for his work on [[pseudospectrum|pseudospectra]] of [[normal matrix|non-normal matrices]] and operators. This work covers theoretical aspects as well as numerical algorithms, and applications including fluid mechanics, numerical solution of partial differential equations, numerical linear algebra, shuffling of cards, random matrices, differential equations and [[lasers]]. Trefethen is currently an [[ISI highly cited researcher]].<ref name="HCR">{{cite web|url=http://highlycited.com/names/t/ |title=T – Research Analytics – Thomson Reuters |publisher=Highlycited.com |date=15 September 2011 |access-date=12 February 2013}}</ref>

Trefethen has written a number of books on numerical analysis including ''Numerical Linear Algebra''<ref>{{cite journal |author=Stewart, G. W. |title=Review: ''Numerical linear algebra'', by L. N. Trefethen and D. Bau |journal=Math. Comp. |year=1999 |volume=68 |issue=225 |pages=453–454 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/mcom/1999-68-225/S0025-5718-99-01069-8/|doi=10.1090/S0025-5718-99-01069-8 |doi-access=free }}</ref> with David Bau, ''Spectral Methods in MATLAB'', ''Schwarz–Christoffel Mapping''  with Tobin Driscoll, and ''Spectra and Pseudospectra: The Behavior of Nonnormal Matrices and Operators''<ref>{{cite journal|author=Higham, Nicholas J.|author-link=Nicholas Higham|title=Review: ''Spectra and pseudospectra: the behavior of nonnormal matrices and operators'', by L. N. Trefethen and M. Embree|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=2007|volume=44|issue=2|pages=277–284|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2007-44-02/S0273-0979-06-01128-1/|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-06-01128-1|doi-access=free}}</ref> with [[Mark Embree]].<ref name="embree"/> He is the leader of the [[MATLAB]]-based [[Chebfun]] software project.

In 2013 he proposed a new formula to calculate the [[body mass index|BMI]] of a person:<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/trefethen/bmi.html | title=New BMI (New Body Mass Index)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.bbc.com/news/magazine-21229387 | title=Does the BMI need correcting?| publisher=BBC News| date=2013-01-29| last1=Stephenson| first1=Wesley}}</ref>

: <math> \text{BMI} = 1.3 \times \frac{\text{weight}\,\,\,\,}{\text{height}^{2.5}}</math>

([[International System of Units]])

===Books===
* ''Numerical Linear Algebra'' (SIAM, 1997) with David Bau
* ''Spectral Methods in Matlab'' (SIAM, 2000)
* ''Schwarz-Christoffel Mapping'' (Cambridge, 2002) with T. A. Driscoll
* ''Spectra and Pseudospectra: The Behavior of Nonnormal Matrices and Operators'' (Princeton, 2005) with Mark Embree
* ''Trefethen's Index Cards'' (World Scientific 2011)
* ''Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice'' (SIAM, 2013 and 2020)
* ''Exploring ODEs'' (SIAM, 2018) with Á. Birkisson and T. A. Driscoll
* ''An Applied Mathematician’s Apology'' (SIAM, 2022)

===Awards and honours===
Trefethen was the first winner of the [[Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis]]. In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Trefethen, Lloyd N.|author2=Driscoll, Tobin A.|chapter=Schwarz-Christoffel mapping in the computer era|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=533–542|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011609000}}</ref> He is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]],<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]. Retrieved 27 August 2013.</ref> and a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in the United States. Trefethen was elected a [[List of fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2005|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2005]],<ref name="royal"/> and his certificate of election reads:

{{blockquote|Nick Trefethen is distinguished for his many seminal contributions to Numerical Analysis and its applications in Applied Mathematics and in Engineering Science. His research spans theory, algorithms, software and physical applications, particularly involving eigenvalues, pseudospectra – a concept which he introduced – and dynamics. He has an international reputation for his work on nonnormal matrices and operators. He has also made major contributions to finite difference and spectral methods for partial differential equations, numerical linear algebra, and complex analysis. His monograph Numerical Linear Algebra (SIAM, 1997) is one of the SIAM's best selling books and has already been through five printings.<ref name="royal"/>}}

In 2010 Trefethen was awarded the [[IMA Gold Medal|Gold Medal]] of the [[Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]] in recognition of his "outstanding contributions to mathematics and its applications over a period of years".<ref>{{cite web|title=IMA Gold Medal|url=https://ima.org.uk/awards-medals/ima-gold-medal/|access-date=16 May 2018}} Institute of Mathematics and its Applications</ref>
In 2013 Trefethen was awarded the [[Naylor Prize]] and lectureship in Applied Mathematics from the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners#Naylor|title=  List of LMS prize winners|publisher= London Mathematical Society|access-date= 25 November 2014}}</ref> He was awarded the George Pólya Prize for Mathematical Exposition in 2017 and the John von Neumann
Prize in 2020 by SIAM.

==Personal life==
Trefethen has one son and one daughter from his first marriage to [[Anne Trefethen|Anne Elizabeth Trefethen]] (née Daman).<ref name="whoswho"/> He is currently married to Kate McLoughlin, a professor of English literature at Oxford.
